The key and the three inside it are the RUNNER's executor-environment vocabulary, not this bundle's: `packages/runner/src/dispatch/resolve-executor-environment.ts` publishes them under these names and `--reference-mode` takes the two mode values verbatim, so renaming them here would declare an input no dispatch delivers

release.description: identifier of what ended up published (commit or tag); filled in when verdict = published

instructions:
# Confirm that the work is published

This step publishes nothing: it **verifies** a publication that already
happened. The whole question is a single one, and it has an objective answer:

> is the merge commit `{{input.artifact.merge_commit}}` contained in the commit
> the running install carries (`{{input.referencia.commit}}`, mode
> `{{input.referencia.modo}}`)?

**Work:** {{input.job.title}} (#{{input.job.id}})

## An honest note about this node

In the reference system this graph ports, this step **never opens an agent
session**: it is a 100% deterministic sweep, because paying a model to run a
sequence of commands with an unambiguous answer is paying for the wrong thing.
This project's graph format does not yet have a "sessionless" node type — and
creating one now, with a single case pressing on the schema, would violate the
rule of two consumers. So the port leaves this node agentic, with 100%
deterministic checks and trivial instructions, and records the divergence
instead of hiding it. When a second real case exists, the new node type arrives
with two consumers to prove the format.

In practice, for you: **do not improvise**. Run this skill's two deterministic
checks, read the exit code and report. There is no judgement to make here, and
anything you "conclude" beyond what the command said is opinion entering a
place where only a fact fitted.

## Where you are

You have read access to the repository (`{{input.project.repo}}`) and no write
access. Do not commit, do not push, do not switch branches, do not touch
another checkout, and do not talk to the network — the verification is local
and historical.

## The procedure

1. **Check that the reference resolves** as a commit in this repository. If it
   does not resolve, the verdict is `undetermined` — it is not "not yet".
2. **Ask the containment question**: is the merge commit an ancestor of the
   reference? Exit 0 is `published`; exit 1 is `not_yet`; any other exit is
   `undetermined`, and you attach the command's output to the note.
3. **Do not force any of the three answers.** `not_yet` is the normal state and
   it resolves itself: the install has not advanced yet, and it will.
   `undetermined` does not resolve itself — the merge commit was rewritten out
   of the history, or the repository is not where it should be — and somebody
   needs to know that. Collapsing the two into one is erasing the only
   difference that matters between them.

This step's trigger is external: nothing here restarts, publishes or promotes
anything. This session observes and reports.

## When to escalate to the human

If you need the founder in order to finish, end your turn with exactly ONE
fenced block, and nothing after it:

```input-request
{"question": "<one or two sentences: what happened and why a decision is needed>",
 "context": "<the supporting detail — evidence, what you tried, the alternatives you weighed>",
 "options": ["<short action label>", "<short action label>"],
 "recommendation": "<the ONE action you would take, in the imperative>",
 "default": "<the option to apply if the founder simply accepts>"}
```

What belongs in each field:

- `question` is read first and has to stay short. State the decision, not the
  investigation that led to it.
- `context` is where ALL of your reasoning goes: the evidence, what you already
  tried, the alternatives you weighed and why you rejected each one. It may run
  long — the founder reads it in full in this session's own record.
- `recommendation` is an imperative action and nothing else — "Run the
  migration, then integrate", not "I think that, since the schema already has
  the column, it would probably be safe to…". It is the text of a one-click
  accept button, so whatever you put there becomes the founder's answer,
  verbatim.
- `options` are short labels, each one a decision the founder could pick.
- `default` is what applies if the founder simply accepts.

Only `question` is required; omit any field that has nothing in it. Ask ONE
question, and do not repeat any of this as prose before or after the block —
the block is the whole message.

Emitting an `input-request` ends your work for now: whatever you have already
done is kept exactly as it is, the session pauses, and the answer reaches you
when it arrives. Do not wait, do not poll, and do not emit two blocks — a
request for a decision always supersedes a report of a result.

Escalate only on the `undetermined` case you cannot explain — `not_yet` is a
normal answer, and a question fired in the normal case is a question the
founder learns to ignore.

## What to return

Return the result in the format this skill's output schema declares: `verdict`,
`checked_reference` (the commit and the mode you actually checked), `note` and,
when the verdict is `published`, also `release` and `deployed_at`.
